Notice the similarity between this observation and the observation we made about composite integration. In section {{REF:1}}, we argued that the error term for a composite integration formula had order one less than that of a single application of the underlying integration formula. The same thing happens here. When the truncation error for the underlying Taylor polynomial has order{{MATH:2}}, the corresponding o.d.e. solver has order {{MATH:3}}, an order equal to the degree of the Taylor polynomial itself.

Taylor's methods and the upcoming Runge-Kutta methods are all designed to work on first order differential equations. However, all the equations of motion we have developed are second order differential equations. To resolve this disconnect, a second order o.d.e. can be reduced to a first order system.
